findings.title: Front-Run Deposits To Steal Pool Tokens
findings.description: This vulnerability allows a malicious pool manager to front-run user deposits by setting the deposit fee close to 100% just before a large deposit is processed. The root cause is the lack of a delay mechanism or upper bound enforcement on fee updates, combined with the absence of slippage protection for users. An attacker (the pool manager) can exploit this by submitting a transaction to increase the fee right before a known large deposit, capturing nearly all of the deposited value as fees, then reducing the fee afterward to avoid detection. The impact is that users can lose a significant portion of their deposit to the pool manager, undermining trust and leading to direct financial loss.

findings.title: Fee Update Delay Bypass
findings.description: This vulnerability allows the pool manager to bypass the intended delay for fee updates by exploiting the timing at epoch boundaries. The root cause is that while certain fees are supposed to only change in the next epoch, the system does not enforce a full epoch delay, allowing the manager to set and apply a new fee immediately at the start of the next epoch. An attacker (again, the pool manager) can exploit this by updating the withdrawal fee at the end of the current epoch and applying it instantly when the new epoch begins, effectively circumventing the intended grace period. The impact is that users are not given sufficient time to react to fee changes, which can lead to unexpected costs and reduced transparency, potentially resulting in economic loss or forced exits under unfavorable conditions.
